haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any Redis call. No rate-limit read or write happens, so no counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: Keys for one customer resolve to the same customer ID and share one counter, so the total is the plan limit: 100 per minute for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. The script increments only when count is below limit, so rejected requests use no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count happens before forwarding and is never rolled back, even when the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway fails open: it forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and returns the backend response without X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per one-minute window. Enterprise is NOT STATED as a number; it is TBD, owned by Product, with no config entry yet.
haiku-low.q8: In the shared Redis primary, under key rl:{customerId}:{windowId}. Each counter expires after 120 seconds, which cleans up old windows.
haiku-low.q9: Fixed clock-aligned one-minute windows: a new window starts a fresh counter. Old counters expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run inside one atomic Lua script that Redis runs without interleaved commands. The gateway never does a separate read then write.
haiku-low.q11: secondsToWindowEnd = 60 - (now mod 60), where now is whole seconds from Redis TIME. The gateway sends it unchanged as Retry-After.
haiku-low.q12: No retry and no local fallback counter. The client gets the backend's normal response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized, returned before any Redis call. No rate-limit read or write, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: Only the one shared limit for the customer's plan per one-minute window (100 for Standard; Enterprise TBD), since all keys resolve to the same customer ID and share one counter.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After: secondsToWindowEnd, X-RateLimit-Limit: limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The backend never sees it; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The script rejects without incrementing, so no budget is used.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count happens before forwarding and is never rolled back, even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: it skips the check, forwards the request to the backend, and increments the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: TBD (open item, owned by Product); not yet decided.
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis instance (primary plus replica; counters read/written on the primary), under key rl:{customerId}:{windowId}. Each counter expires after 120 s, which cleans up old windows.
sonnet.q9: When the one-minute clock-aligned window ends, a new window starts with a fresh counter (new windowId), so the budget starts from zero. Old counters expire after 120 s.
sonnet.q10: The check and increment run inside one atomic Lua script on Redis, which runs without other commands in between. The gateway never does a separate read then write, so two instances cannot both read 99 and proceed.
sonnet.q11: The script returns secondsToWindowEnd = 60 - (now mod 60), with now being whole seconds from Redis TIME. It is always 1 to 60, and the gateway sends it unchanged as Retry-After.
sonnet.q12: No retry and no local fallback counter in v1. The client gets the backend's normal response with no X-RateLimit-* headers, since the real values are unknown.
